findings.claim: The spike settled the cross-marketplace risk at user scope only, but the done-when test (install into a scratch repository) and the --scope project path are untested. At project scope it is open which scope the scaccogatto and kmctl marketplaces must be declared at (claude plugin marketplace add --scope project|user), whether okf resolves and installs at project scope when its marketplace is declared there, and whether a teammate who clones the repo gets both. If dependency resolution only sees user-scope marketplaces, or okf lands at user scope, the project-scope design changes. A spike should answer: with an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and a scratch repo, does `marketplace add --scope project` for both marketplaces followed by `plugin install --scope project` install okf at project scope, and is a second run a no-op?

The plan does not say where kmctl's marketplace comes from, yet the intent rests on it: the plugin must come from the same release as the CLI (ADR 0001). Adding the repo at GitHub HEAD gives a plugin that can differ from the installed CLI; a path inside the installed wheel needs the plugin packaged into the wheel (pyproject has no such data today) and breaks when the environment moves (uvx caches, upgrades), since folder plugins load in place; a git ref (#vX.Y.Z) needs release tags. The choice also decides what 'a second install changes nothing' and 'plugin status against this CLI's version' mean when a marketplace of the same name is already added at a different version or source. Name the source and how an existing mismatched marketplace is handled before building; if a pinned ref is the answer, a spike should check that `claude plugin marketplace add owner/repo#ref` pins and that re-adding at a new ref updates rather than errors.
Project scope was untested. Spike plugin-install-verb/3 shows it pulls okf, that reruns keep the same settings content, and that a teammate must run the install once. The plan records all three.
The source of kmctl's marketplace was not decided. The plan now ships plugin/ and the marketplace as package data, stages them locally and never uses GitHub HEAD.

The upgrade path is untested, and the plan departs from loopctl here. The plan names the staging folder by kmctl's version, so a newer kmctl moves the marketplace to a new path while Claude Code still has the kmctl marketplace registered at the old one. Nothing shows that `claude plugin marketplace add <new path>` under an existing name exits 0 and points the marketplace at the new path, or that `plugin install` then picks up the new version. Spike 3's rerun says 'already installed' and loads in place, which suggests it may not. loopctl does not do this: it stages to one fixed path (data_dir()/marketplace), falls back to `marketplace update` when add fails, and uninstalls before reinstalling on update (commands/plugin.py _install_claude). At project scope, a version-named path also rewrites the committed .claude/settings.json on every release. The plan should either use loopctl's fixed path or settle this with a spike. Spike question: with a directory marketplace already registered at path A (plugin version 0.0.1), does `marketplace add B` (same marketplace name, plugin 0.0.2) followed by `plugin install --scope user|project` exit 0, leave the marketplace at B, and make `plugin list --json` report 0.0.2? If not, what sequence does (marketplace remove/update, plugin uninstall, or plugin update)?
Project scope was untested; spike 3 settles it and the plan records the teammate limit.
The plugin source is package data staged locally, never GitHub HEAD.

The version-named staging folder is replaced by loopctl's fixed marketplace/ folder and its add, update-on-fail, uninstall-on-update, install, list --json order; done-when now tests an update to a bumped version at the same path.

status() reads folderVersion (and the staged copy) instead of the version claude lists, so the install post-check always equals cli_version and is dead. After a kmctl upgrade, `kmctl plugin install` exits 0 and reports plugin 0.2.0 while `claude plugin list --json` shows kmctl@kmctl at version 0.1.0 with only the 0.1.0 cache dir, and `kmctl plugin status` reports no problem.

install() skips adding scaccogatto when any scope already knows it, so a project-scope install in a second repo, or for a user who already has scaccogatto at user scope, writes enabledPlugins okf@scaccogatto to .claude/settings.json with no extraKnownMarketplaces entry for scaccogatto. The plan says the project settings file lists both marketplaces.

_listed() returns the first kmctl@kmctl entry, whatever its scope or projectPath. claude lists project-scope installs from other repos (enabled false), so in a repo with no install, status reports 'version mismatch ... run kmctl plugin update' from another repo's entry instead of 'not installed; run kmctl plugin install'. The install post-check can also read the wrong entry.

r1's test never checks that the kmctl and okf entries are at the chosen scope, though fails_when says 'at that scope'. r2's test compares only kmctl's version, not the whole plugin list as fails_when says, and never checks the first install's exit code.

_report is typed `result: object`, so mypy reports 4 new errors (asdict overload and attr-defined at __init__.py:485-490). It should take PluginStatus. Two older mypy errors remain (review_due.py:120, __init__.py:318).

entries.change: status uses the version claude lists for the entry, not the staged copy, and reports a staged mismatch separately; install declares the scaccogatto marketplace at the chosen scope every time; entries are matched by scope and, for project scope, by project path, so other repositories' installs are ignored.
_report takes PluginStatus, and the concept verb table is typed tuple[Kind, str] so mypy accepts it.
_last_verified filters parsed dates into a separate list[datetime] so max() type-checks.

r1 checks both plugins are project scope for this repository, r2 checks the first install's exit code and compares the whole plugin list, and new tests cover okf declared in a second repository and status ignoring another repository's install.

findings.claim: status() now reads `version` from the matching claude list entry, and a staged-copy mismatch is a separate problem.
install() declares scaccogatto at the chosen scope on every run.
_entry() filters by scope and, for project scope, by projectPath equal to cwd; project wins over user.
r1 asserts scope and projectPath for both ids; r2 asserts the first exit code and compares every listed plugin's version and scope.
_report takes PluginStatus and the older mypy errors are fixed; only the missing yaml stubs remain.

After a kmctl upgrade without update, status lists two problems with different fixes: 'installed plugin 0.2.0 ... run kmctl plugin update' and 'staged plugin 0.2.0 ... run kmctl plugin install'. Following the second runs install, which now refuses with 'run kmctl plugin update'. The staged-copy hint should name update when the installed version is also behind (or be left out then).

No test covers the f1 fix: a plain install over an older installed version must exit 1 naming kmctl plugin update, and status must report the installed-version mismatch. r5's test only edits the staged copy, so it passes even if the installed-version check is removed.

entries.change: A staged-copy mismatch now says run kmctl plugin update, the same fix as an installed mismatch, so status never points at an install that would refuse.
A test installs, bumps the CLI version, and checks status reports the installed mismatch with only the update fix, a plain install refuses naming update, and update clears it.
